info.desc: Talking Heads: 77 is the debut album by American rock band Talking Heads. It was recorded in April 1977 at New York's Sundragon Studios and released on September 16 of that year by Sire Records. The single Psycho Killer reached number 92 on the Billboard Hot 100. Recording: After developing a following playing lower Manhattan's CBGB scene, Talking Heads shopped demos they had recorded for record labels, eventually signing a deal with Sire Records in late 1976. The following April, the band began recording the album at Sundragon Studios, a small studio in lower Manhattan. Release history: Sire Records in .

podcast.body: This debut album was released in 1977. Its sound, and New Wave in general, was perceived as refreshing compared to the soft rock offerings prevalent on FM radio at the time, which included songs by Debbie Boone, Carly Simon, Shaun Cassidy, and KC and the Sunshine Band. "When the Bee Gees were taking the number one spot from Debbie Boone and I get it that the Bee Gees were part and parcel of the commercialization of disco, the Talking Heads were releasing their first album and there were some changes afoot."
